Subject: POC Kickoff Recap & Next Steps

Hi Alicia / Ben —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the proposed plan for the 2-week POC so we stay aligned: 

Summary of goals (proposed success criteria):
- Integrations: Ingest Acme transaction + metadata feed into Redwood in under 24 hours (sample 1M rows)
- Latency: 95th percentile end-to-end inference latency < 250ms for your typical prompt set
- Cost/throughput: Demonstrate batching that reduces per-token cost by >=20% vs baseline
- Quality: Customer-defined 5 key prompts produce outputs meeting your accuracy/format checks >= 85%

Proposed timeline:
- Week 0 (this week): access & environment setup, sample data push
- Week 1: baseline tests, tuning (batching/quantization suggestions), run eval set
- Week 2: final tuning, demo, success criteria review + next steps

Ownership & asks: 
- Acme: provide sample dataset (CSV or Parquet), test account or synthetic data, point of contact for infra (Ben)
- Redwood: SE ownership (Marcus) to set up staging, Marissa to run MAP and coordinate demos

Attachments: draft mutual action plan and evaluation template attached.

Action items for you: please confirm the success criteria above and whether the proposed 2-week timeline works. Also confirm who will provide the sample data and who from IT can approve network access.

Thanks — looking forward to getting started.

Best,

Hi team — quick technical checklist from my side to get the staging POC up: 

1) Data: sanitized sample (CSV/Parquet) + schema. If possible include a small subset (10k rows) for initial smoke tests.
2) Network: either a temporary s3 bucket we can access (pre-signed URL) or a staging VM with SSH + firewall rules.
3) Workloads: please share the 5 canonical prompts, typical sequence length, and expected concurrency (requests/sec).

Notes on environment: Redwood can run the model in your VPC (private deployment) or in our dedicated staging environment. For speed, recommended path is to provide S3 access and let us ingest; if Acme requires VPC peering we'll need to schedule a short network call with Ben.
